project.name: research-domain-writing
project.identity: A broadly reusable research-grounded writing quality layer for consequential prose across Career Ops outreach, resumes, cover letters, application answers, emails, messages, social content, reports, and product copy.
project.audience: People and agents producing consequential prose across career, communication, research, reporting, and product workflows.
project.core_loop: Research the task, assemble a source-backed packet, draft the prose, run domain-aware quality checks, obtain human approval, and retain a content-bound receipt without taking ownership of runtime enforcement.
project.north_star: Consequential prose remains grounded, calibrated, channel-appropriate, and reviewable across domains instead of merely sounding polished.
not_this: A generic content generator detached from sources and domain
The runtime enforcement owner for Career Ops or other consuming systems

mvp.definition: A standalone deterministic CLI proves a bounded research packet to draft to domain-QA to receipt lifecycle for one domain task without claiming a general LLM runtime.

complete_product.definition: A broadly reusable writing-quality layer serves the declared Career Ops, communication, research, reporting, and product-copy workflows with domain packs, reviewable evidence, and explicit integration boundaries.

outcomes.name: Consequential prose can be checked for source grounding, calibration, channel fit, and domain quality before human approval.

layers.intended: The quality layer is reusable across Career Ops outreach, resumes, cover letters, application answers, emails, messages, social content, reports, and product copy.
layers.planned: The project documents research packets, domain-aware prompts or checks, deterministic fixtures, and deferred integrations.
layers.implemented: The current standalone CLI and domain-pack implementation prove a bounded task lifecycle and artifact receipt.
layers.verified: Repository evidence supports the standalone lifecycle; the broad cross-domain integration outcome and runtime enforcement parity are not verified here.
